text:
Nina: Quick heads-up  Aster Bank (enterprise pilot) needs per-endpoint SLA + explicit invoice caps. They want ability to purchase an 'endpoint-priority' add-on and set a hard throughput ceiling per endpoint.
Sam: Clarify: are they asking for two separate products (priority lane + hard cap) or one combined SKU?
Nina: Ideally both. They want to buy priority for mission-critical endpoints, and separately enforce caps on public endpoints to limit noisy usage.
Elena: Contract/Legal note: we need fallback language for when priority lane saturates. They insist on defined remedies & credit calc.
Tom: Implementation constraints: billing currently only supports account-level line items. We'll need mapping so invoice lines can show endpoint_id. Minimal approach: tag usage exports with endpoint_id and join in billing pipeline.
Priya: Launch criteria proposal:
- M1: API flag to opt-in endpoints for priority or cap
- M2: Billing line items per endpoint for invoices in beta accounts
- M3: Contract template + credit calc for SLA misses
- M4: Ops runbook for priority exhaustion and automatic fallback
Sam: Timebox: if we ship minimal UX (flag + invoice mapping + contract), we can target 6 weeks. If they need self-serve UI for add-on purchase, +3w.
Elena: Credit calc example we discussed: credits = min(max(0, SLA_hit_deficit) * multiplier, monthly_endpoint_spend)  — legal wants the multiplier documented. Suggest 1.2x.
Tom: Technical checklist (short):
```
- add endpoint_id to usage export
- add invoice mapping: endpoint_id -> line_item_code
- api param: endpoint_priority = {none, baseline, priority}
- enforcement: quota service enforces hard cap per endpoint
```
Priya: Risks:
- Billing reconciliation complexity for multi-route customers
- Accounting needs to map credits to GL codes
- UI/ops overhead if lots of endpoints are purchased
Nina: Negotiation stance: offer a limited pilot (3 endpoints) as an enterprise add-on. Full self-serve later.
Sam: Pricing thought: baseline add-on = $X/month per endpoint (soft guarantee), priority lane = premium per qps or flat reserved qps. We should model both: flat vs usage-based.
Elena: Also call out contract constraint: endpoint names/IDs must be enumerated in the order form. No dynamic endpoints without amendment.
Tom: Ops: will need an incident playbook if priority lane drops below SLA; include automatic credits & escalation to SRE.
account-bot: Billing epic created: https://redwood.internal/epics/endpoint-sla-billing (link)
Priya: Action items: Nina to lock pilot scope with Aster; Tom to spike billing export (2d); Sam to draft pricing scenarios (flat vs usage); Elena to draft contract clause; Priya to write launch checklist.
Nina: I'll sync with Aster this afternoon and push for pilot only on 3 production endpoints.
Sam: FYI adding this to the pricing board under "endpoint-sla pilot".
Nina: Thanks everyone. Closing for now.
